passage: A storm rattled the windows and the power went out, so the flat was black except for a candle Mummy Mridul had lit. Eshaan lay stiff in bed. Dadi had died last month. "Mummy," he whispered, "will you die too?" Mridul did not laugh or say never mind. She sat on the bed and took his hand. "Someday, everyone does, but most people live a very long time. I am healthy and I plan to be here for a long time. And if something happened, you would be looked after." His shoulders loosened, and he pulled her hand under his chin.

qa.q: What happened to the power in the flat?
qa.a: The power went out during a storm.

qa.q: What was Eshaan feeling when he whispered his question?
qa.a: Eshaan was frightened, especially in the dark after Dadi's death. Lying stiff and whispering show how afraid he was.

qa.q: What did Mridul do that helped Eshaan feel calmer?
qa.a: She answered honestly and calmly, said most people live a long time, and told him he would always be looked after. She did not hide from the question or lie.

qa.q: How might Mridul feel when Eshaan asks whether she will die?
qa.a: Mridul may feel a pang, since the question is heavy, but she wants to reassure him. She chose to be truthful and steady instead of avoiding it.

grounding: A child asks whether his mother will die too and feels frightened at night, and honest calm answers help, while hiding the question would make the fear bigger.
